findings.where: Whole lesson (STEPS, explain, practice) against the brief's lesson 5 row
findings.what: The brief promises Pascal's principle and the hydraulic jack (100 N on 10 cm² lifting 2000 N on 200 cm², the small piston moving 20 times as far so work in equals work out), the U-tube manometer, barometer and Bourdon gauge, and relative density, but none of them appear anywhere and no later lesson takes them, because the lesson prompt never carried that row; add a hydraulic-jack SHOW and DO pair (and relative density as one line on screen 10), or move the gauges explicitly into lesson 7's row where pressure reads as head.

It says the 10.1 kN 'equals the weight of the seawater the cube pushes aside' without the step that makes it so (the extra pressure is ρg × 1 m acting on 1 m², which is ρg × 1 m³, and 1 m³ of seawater is 1025 kg, weighing 1025 × 9.81 ≈ 10.1 kN); a steps lesson shows only its screens, so this central Archimedes step rests on an unlabelled bar.

findings.where: Screen 10 'Float, hover or sink', text (feeds screen 11 'A pontoon')
findings.what: The draughts 0.59 m and 0.60 m are given without the working (600 kg must push aside 600 kg of seawater, 600 ÷ 1025 ≈ 0.59 m³, which on a 1 m² base is 0.59 m deep), yet the very next puzzle asks him to do that sum for the pontoon; add the working and split the screen in two if it would pass about 90 words (it is 89 now).

'Its weight is ρ × h × 1 m² × g, where ρ is the density, the mass in each cubic metre.' packs two ideas into a 21-word clause chain; split it: 'ρ is the density, the mass in each cubic metre. The column weighs ρ × h × 1 m² × g.'

The lesson carries eight footnote markers, with [^3] on 'pressure comes from the weight of the liquid above' and [^4] on the definition of density, general statements he would never look up, and [^5] twice; keep them to seawater's density, 10 m ≈ one atmosphere, Archimedes' rule once and the HSE isolation step.
Fresh water's 1000 kg/m³ has no source, and the brief lists it as still to cite; add a cited constant to research and point the number at it.

findings.where: Screen 2 at 360 px, light and dark moved shots
findings.what: Numbers split from their units at line ends ('1' / 'm²', '100.6' / 'kPa'); put non-breaking spaces between numbers and units in the screen text.

findings.where: Screen 2 'The weight above', Fresh water switch
findings.what: The screen has a Fresh water switch that its words never mention; add one sentence (each metre of fresh water adds a little less) or leave the switch to screen 10.

findings.where: Lead paragraph and caption, every screen
findings.what: The lead ('Three joined tanks of seawater filled to one level, an example 10 m deep, ...') is a fragment with an aside, and it shows on all 13 screens, including the warm-up, cube, pontoon, sensor and float screens it does not describe; the fixed caption also gives p = ρgh on the warm-up before screen 2 teaches it.
'Drag the probe down any tank.' but the ring only changes depth and the tank is chosen with the Tank buttons; say 'Pick a tank, then drag the probe down.'
The probe jumps from tank to tank, and its face flips, with nothing in between (step keys); a short slide or fade would read as one probe moving rather than popping.
Absolute pressure is lesson 3's term but is highlighted in amber and defined again as if new; refer back to it ('as with the air receiver') instead.
'0.50 m' lacks the 'About' that the other two choices carry; make the three consistent.
The steel-hull idea (overall density is mass ÷ all the space the outside encloses) lives only in explain and practice; one sentence on screen answers 'big heavy things sink' for a ship.

The only pictures of the cube screens are contact sheets too small to read, so the builder and this review checked their labels from the drawing code (no overlaps found at top 2, 6 or 7 m, nor floating or sunk), not by eye.
